findings.message: Rule-bearing legacy code in Procurement.Rules.approvalLimits matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). Superseded authority: numeric literal 7500.00 (line 7): value 7500.00 = DEC-PR01.p1 (superseded by DEC-PR04, same form) and no accepted parameter has the same form. Supported (matching rule): numeric literal 40000.00 (line 8): (b) parameter, value 40000.00 = DEC-PR04.p2 (accepted, same form). The code still carries a superseded decision's value. Question for Finance Controller: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.

Rule-bearing legacy code in Procurement.Rules.|ApprovedSoleSource|_| matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). No accepted authority: category test '= "LabReagents"' (line 22): no accepted record names "LabReagents". Supported (matching rule): category test '= "V-3302"' (line 22): (c) comment citation, "V-3302" is named by accepted APR-PR01, cited in the declaration's comment. A category test treats one category differently (a possible exemption); a record that names the category must authorize it. Question for Dana Whitlock, Chief Procurement Officer: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.

Rule-bearing legacy code in Procurement.Rules.bidsRequired matches no observation and has rule-bearing constructs without accepted authority (ast analyzer). No accepted authority: case keyed on ApprovedSoleSource (line 28): no accepted record names ApprovedSoleSource; numeric literal 1 (line 28): value 1 equals no declared parameter of an accepted or superseded record; case keyed on ContractRenewal (line 29): no accepted record names ContractRenewal; numeric literal 1 (line 29): value 1 equals no declared parameter of an accepted or superseded record; wildcard default returning 1 for unlisted cases (line 31): value 1 equals no declared parameter of an accepted or superseded record. A wildcard default silently decides every unlisted case; no record authorizes that default. A category test treats one category differently (a possible exemption); a record that names the category must authorize it. Question for praxis-intake: which accepted record, if any, authorizes it? New work must not reuse it until answered; the legacy code is left unchanged.
